transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-21
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Sandbar Head of ML), Owen Clarke (Sandbar Platform), Sasha Kim (Sandbar Privacy)

Summary: quick POC sync to review tokens/sec per dollar, caching impact seen in the past week, and batching/latency tradeoffs. Decide next bench runs and share artifacts (benchmark sheet link).
Topics: tokens/sec/$, prefix/KV cache savings, batching config, dedicated vs hosted latency, data residency note

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: alright everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 45 minutes, we wanted to go over the economics snapshot and next bench runs. Marco and I will take the first half, then open floor for questions.
[00:18] Priya Nair: great, thanks Lena. quick status — we ran the 1k prompt set overnight, saw overall token spend about 12% lower than the first week, but latency variance is still a thing.
[00:31] Marco Ruiz: yeah that matches what we saw in the dashboard. to be explicit; tokens per dollar improved because of the prefix cache hits - roughly 28% hit-rate for the last 24 hours on the short prompt family, which saved about 14% of tokens overall.
[00:46] Owen Clarke: is that the KV cache or the prefix cache? we got mixed terms internally.
[00:52] Marco Ruiz: sorry, that's prefix caching — so when you have the same few conversation opens or system prompts we don't re-run them; KV cache is the per-request keyvalue store in the LLM runtime for generative context, those are separate. sometimes the export labels them as K-V cache or K-Vcach, which is confusing.
[01:12] Sasha Kim: just flagging for privacy: are cached entries encrypted at rest? the SOC docs we reviewed were a bit high-level.
[01:18] Lena Park: good call — yes, cached payloads in the hosted pilot are encrypted at rest with our KMS by default; for Private we can map to customer KMS/HSM. we'll attach the SOC2 page and KMS note after the call.
[01:32] Priya Nair: perfect. can you quickly walk through tokens/sec/$ math? we want the raw formula to plug into our finance model.
[01:38] Marco Ruiz: sure — simple way is tokens per second divided by dollars per second. dollars per second = (price per token * tokens per second) so that cancels — but for batch-aware workloads we break it into tokens per batch / seconds per batch / cost per batch. Practically we publish tokens/sec/$ for each model variant in the sheet. For our thin-quantized variant we saw about 1.9x tokens/sec/$ vs the fat baseline on A100-ish hardware in the hosted pool.
[02:05] Owen Clarke: that 1.9x — is that including the effects of caching?
[02:09] Marco Ruiz: yes that included observed prefix cache savings. raw compute-only was about 1.3x. caching amplified the unit econ.
[02:17] Priya Nair: what about batching? we tried increasing batch size to 8 and saw better tokens/sec but latency tails went up beyond our 500ms SLO for interactive flows.
[02:29] Lena Park: exactly — tradeoff. batching improves throughput (and thus tokens/sec/$) but increases median and tail latency. for interactive you can use micro-batching or dynamic batching with a small latency budget, or use a dedicated low-latency pool.
[02:44] Sasha Kim: any quantitative numbers we can point to? what's the tokens/sec/$ at batch 1 vs batch 8 for the quantized model?
[02:52] Marco Ruiz: in our run, quantized model at batch 1: 120 tokens/sec/$; batch 8: 420 tokens/sec/$ but p95 latency jumped from ~220ms to ~720ms. those are rough, depends on prompt lengths.
[03:08] Priya Nair: that's useful. do these runs include the KV cache warm-up? some sessions were cold.
[03:15] Marco Ruiz: good point — the numbers I quoted are steady-state after warm-up. cold-start penalizes both tokens/sec and latency; that's where prefix caching helps most for repeated system prompts.
[03:24] Owen Clarke: we ran a baseline on our side in EU region and observed slightly worse tokens/sec — suspect network egress plus smaller instance types. is it possible to pin a dedicated capacity in EU for us to test?
[03:36] Lena Park: yes, Dedicated can be provisioned in EU. we can reserve a small dedicated pool to match your instance class; that would stabilize latency and predictable throughput. pricing differs since it is reserved. I'll include a sample price for a small committed pool in the follow-up.
[03:50] Priya Nair: about quantization — we saw a quality delta on the few-shot long-context prompts. can you recommend quant bits or a mixed strategy?
[03:58] Marco Ruiz: we've had success with 4-bit SG-QAT for short to medium context. for long context you might want mixed precision: keep attention and KV in higher precision, quantize the feedforward. that preserves quality while reducing cost. We can provide a recommended profile for your prompt family.
[04:15] Sasha Kim: does quantization change caching behavior? like does the cached token align across variants?
[04:21] Marco Ruiz: cached prefixes are normalized to a canonical tokenization layer before storage, so if your model variants share that tokenization (most do) the cache is compatible. slight differences can happen if you change the tokenizer or model family.
[04:34] Priya Nair: ok, good. we'd like to push more of our conversational traffic to the cache-friendly flow, but some of our elite users need the freshest weights and can't tolerate quant artifacts. is there routing support between variants?
[04:46] Lena Park: yes — smart routing policy lets you send traffic by tag, by user segment, or fallback rules. e.g., 90% to quantized variant, 10% to high-fidelity variant for A/B. plus auto-fallback if the quantized variant fails validation.
[05:01] Owen Clarke: curious about the billing model for hybrid routing — do you get charged per invocation variant used?
[05:07] Lena Park: yes billing maps to the model variant actually served; routing doesn't change billing other than what was invoked. we can show an expected blended tokens/sec/$ for the split you choose.
[05:19] Priya Nair: we have a question on disk and cache retention — how long do caches live in the hosted pilot? we want to keep short-lived system prompts cached for 1 hour, but nothing persistent beyond that for compliance.
[05:31] Marco Ruiz: default TTL in the pilot is 24h but configurable; for Sandbar we can set prefix cache TTL to 1h. also you can disable caching for sessions tagged "sensitive".
[05:41] Sasha Kim: perfect. that'll help with our data retention policy.
[05:45] Lena Park: quick note — I uploaded the latest benchmark sheet here: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/sandbar-pilot (shared). it has the token/sec/$ chart by variant, region and batch size.
[05:58] Priya Nair: thanks, I'll open it after the call. can you also add sample prompt-level cost lines so our finance team can run a P&L on projected MAU?
[06:08] Lena Park: yes will do.
[06:12] Marco Ruiz: back to the numbers — one interesting signal: enabling prefix caching and micro-batching together yielded about 35% extra savings vs enabling either alone for the short-turn prompts. dynamic batching where we cap latency at 350ms gave a reasonable middle ground.
[06:29] Owen Clarke: hmm okay, for the interactive product we probably need median < 250ms. is that achievable with micro-batching and a hot KV cache?
[06:36] Marco Ruiz: feasible on Dedicated in region with a smaller batch horizon. the trick is keep batch size small and warm the KV/prefix cache for known patterns. for unknown prompts you'll still see higher latency.
[06:47] Priya Nair: any tooling to estimate percentage of traffic that will be cache-friendly?
[06:52] Marco Ruiz: yes — we provide a small evaluator script you can run against historical traffic to estimate repeatable prefixes and expected cache hit-rate. I can drop that script in the sheet.
[07:02] Sasha Kim: send that please. also reminder — Sandbar needs SAML SSO and RBAC mapping for our pilot team. where are we on that?
[07:09] Lena Park: SSO is in progress; we have SAML for the console and RBAC roles can be mapped. Marco, can you note the open infra tasks?
[07:18] Marco Ruiz: noted — SAML config pending on Sandbar's IdP details; session timeout and RBAC policy mapping will be scheduled. I'll add the task to the action items.
[07:27] Owen Clarke: last technical thing — network. do you recommend VPC peering or Private deployment? given we have strict egress and want audit logs.
[07:36] Lena Park: if audit logs and KMS integration are top priorities, Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) gives you full control and mapping to your KMS and SIEM. VPC peering is a middle ground where control plane is Redwood hosted but data plane routes over the peering link. We can outline both options.
[07:51] Priya Nair: costs and timeline? Private looks heavier.
[07:55] Lena Park: Private is heavier (longer lead time and license), Dedicated with VPC peering is a faster middle lane. I'll include an estimated timeline and cost comparison in the follow-up.
[08:06] Priya Nair: sounds good. on the pilot metrics — what's a realistic tokens/sec/$ target for us if we go Dedicated + micro-batching + 4-bit quant?
[08:16] Marco Ruiz: ballpark: 3x the fat baseline in steady-state for short prompts, assuming a decent cache hit-rate (30%+). that's using Dedicated hardware comparable to A100 class.
[08:27] Owen Clarke: and what's the expected p95 latency then?
[08:30] Marco Ruiz: likely in the 260-380ms range with micro-batching and warm cache; specifics depend on prompt length distribution.
[08:38] Sasha Kim: are there concerns with regen or safety checks adding cost? we run content filtering after generation.
[08:44] Lena Park: safety checks add tokens for the moderation pass — if you run them as separate invocations that doubles that part's token cost; you can also do inline filter hooks which are more efficient. the sheet includes examples for moderation-on vs moderation-off costs.
[08:59] Priya Nair: good to know. can you include an example monthly projection for 10M interactions with mixed routing?
[09:05] Lena Park: yes, we'll add a projection with the 90/10 split scenario and show blended tokens/sec/$.
[09:11] Marco Ruiz: one more technical note — when you use mixed model routing the cache is per model family. if you route to two different families, you'll have separate cache namespaces; if they're the same family but different quantization the cache is compatible as I mentioned earlier.
[09:27] Owen Clarke: thanks Marco.
[09:30] Priya Nair: quick process question — after you share the sheet and the KV traces, what's the expected timeline to finalize pilot adjustments and then move to a short dedicated trial?
[09:40] Lena Park: proposal: we share artifacts by Tues (2026-03-24), Sandbar runs targeted prompts by Thurs (2026-03-26), we reconvene for a latency-dedicated bench and pricing sign-off the week of 2026-03-30.
[09:56] Priya Nair: that timeline works for us.
[09:59] Sasha Kim: ok. please ensure we have the compliance bits attached (SOC2, KMS mapping, data retention SLA).
[10:06] Lena Park: will do.
[10:08] Marco Ruiz: I'll also include a short how-to for the evaluator script and an example command to estimate cache hit rates from your logs.
[10:17] Owen Clarke: another small request — can you provide a shot of throughput vs cost at different concurrency levels? our ops team wants concurrency numbers not just batch size.
[10:27] Marco Ruiz: yes, concurrent connections vs batching interplay can be confusing; I'll add a graph for concurrency 10/50/200 with typical instance shapes.
[10:36] Priya Nair: thanks. any blockers from your side?
[10:40] Lena Park: none besides IdP details for SAML and confirmation of the EU region preference for the Dedicated trial.
[10:47] Priya Nair: we'll confirm IdP and EU region by end of day tomorrow.
[10:51] Lena Park: perfect. recap and next steps — we'll share the benchmark sheet, pricing examples for Dedicated and reserved pool, KV/prefix cache logs, evaluator script, and compliance docs by 2026-03-24. Sandbar will run the targeted prompts and return results by 2026-03-26. schedule Dedicated bench the week of 2026-03-30.
[11:15] Priya Nair: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[11:18] Lena Park: thanks all, talk soon.

References/Artifacts:
- Benchmark sheet (shared): https://redwood.app/benchmarks/sandbar-pilot
- KV/prefix cache log export (to be attached)
- Evaluator script (will be added to sheet)

End of transcript.
